bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is an AI subfield focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern technology for image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Recent growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised Learning, Unsupervised Learning, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trains on labeled data to predict continuous (regression) or categorical (classification) outputs.
Unsupervised Learning: Finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data using techniques like clustering or dimensionality reduction.
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards, used in robotics and gaming.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split to train the model and evaluate its performance on unseen data.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor generalization.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicting class probabilities.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane for classification, effective in high-dimensional spaces.
Neural Networks: Brain-inspired models capable of learning complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, and algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, and safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Evaluate model performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, MSE, R-squared.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data by splitting into multiple subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance using methods like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Complex models can be difficult to understand, especially in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair or unethical outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting a model's ability to generalize.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased integration into daily life across healthcare, education, entertainment, and transportation.
Growing importance of ethical considerations and responsible AI practices as the field progresses.
